title: I Built My First Multi-Agent System on AWS, and It Was Easier Than I Expected
why_read: A hands-on writeup of building a multi-agent AWS system using Bedrock AgentCore and Strands Agents gives a concrete, practical look at current agentic AI tooling patterns.
analysis: This describes a student project building a multi-agent customer support system with an orchestrator coordinating four specialized agents sharing state through DynamoDB. It touches on real AWS services and patterns like Bedrock Guardrails, optimistic locking for concurrent state updates, and distributed tracing with X-Ray. While it's a course project rather than production system, the architectural pattern of orchestrator plus specialized agents with shared workflow state is a useful, concrete example of current multi-agent design. The writing is promotional in tone and lacks deep technical analysis of tradeoffs, limiting its depth for experienced practitioners.
